name: Command Hold
description:
Hold a key and say what to do. Offline voice commands for GNOME.

Hold the shortcut (Super+C by default), speak, release: "open Firefox", "volume 50", "dark mode", "next workspace", "lock the screen", "screenshot", "Wi-Fi off"… run at once. Anything else ("clone the repo owner slash name", "update the system", "what is using my memory") becomes a shell command that you see and confirm before it runs in a visible terminal; the pill then reports done or failed.

Everything runs on your computer: speech recognition by the Voice Hold engine (French, English and 23 other languages), GNOME actions by rules, open requests by a small local LLM through Ollama (optional). No account, no cloud.

Requires the separate command-hold-engine helper (Python, GPL, one command to install) and the Voice Hold engine; nothing works without them. The settings page shows the install commands, with a button that copies them to the clipboard, and the engine status. Wayland only.
